title: No tax on tips? Not quite. Myth vs fact
label: Tax myth vs fact

hook.sub: Tax myth vs fact, for 2025 to 2028.

items.l: Tips aren't taxed at all now
Social Security and Medicare still apply

items.s: Servers, bartenders, salon workers and more.

items.t: You need a Social Security number

beats.sub: Some service businesses can't use it.

cta.sub: We'll DM you how to book a call.

captions.instagram:
"No tax on tips" is a deduction, not a pass on all tax.

✔️ For 2025 through 2028, you can deduct up to $25,000 of qualified tips a year, whether or not you itemize.
✔️ It's for jobs where tips are customary, like servers, bartenders and salon workers. Tips must be voluntary, and you need a Social Security number.
✔️ It starts phasing out above $150,000 of modified AGI ($300,000 joint).
✔️ Social Security and Medicare still apply to reported tips.
✔️ Self-employed? It can't be more than your profit from that business, and some service businesses can't use it.

captions.youtube_description: For 2025 through 2028, workers in tipped occupations can deduct up to $25,000 of qualified (voluntary) tips a year, itemizing or not, with a Social Security number. Self-employed: capped at the profit from that business, and some service businesses are excluded.

sources.fact: No tax on tips: maximum $25,000 a year; voluntary cash or charged tips; phases out over $150,000 MAGI ($300,000 joint); available whether or not you itemize; self-employed: can't exceed net income from that business (page updated 21-Sep-2026); read 2026-10-30

Tips deduction effective 2025 through 2028; occupations customarily receiving tips as of Dec. 31, 2024; SSN required; SSTB self-employed and employees excluded (page updated 27-Aug-2026); read 2026-10-30

Employers withhold Social Security and Medicare on reported tips; the new qualified tips deduction ($25,000, 2025-2028) is described for income tax withholding only (Topic 761, updated 12-Oct-2026); read 2026-10-30
